units.meaning: Provides administrative metadata regarding the Foreign Affairs Manual amendment and date, with no substantive operational rule.
Defines a material discrepancy as any name change that does not qualify as immaterial under 8 FAM 403.1-5.

source_spans.quote: A material discrepancy is any name change that is not defined as immaterial in 8 FAM 403.1-5.

units.meaning: Applicants are required to explain any material discrepancies between the name provided on the application and the name shown in the citizenship/nationality evidence and identity evidence, referencing 22 CFR 51.25.

source_spans.quote: The applicant must explain any material discrepancies between the name on the application and the name recorded in the evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality and the evidence of identity (see 22 CFR 51.25).

units.meaning: An applicant must document material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application and the name in citizenship/nationality or identity evidence by submitting one or more of the documents listed in 8 FAM 403.1-4, unless the exception for married names under 8 FAM 403.1-4(C) applies.

source_spans.quote: Material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application, the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality, or the evidence of identity must be documented by submission of one or more of the documents listed in this section (see an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C)).

units.meaning: An exception to the requirement for documenting material name discrepancies applies to married names under 8 FAM 403.1-4(C).

source_spans.quote: (see an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C))

units.meaning: Declares the Department's principle that an applicant's name forms an integral part of their identity.

source_spans.quote: The applicant's name is an integral part of her/his identity.

units.meaning: Pursuant to 22 CFR 51.23(c) and Department guidance, the Department may require evidence of identity to establish the name that best identifies the applicant.

source_spans.quote: Consequently, under 22 CFR 51.23(c), evidence of identity might be required in accordance with Department guidance to establish the name that best identifies the applicant:

units.meaning: If an applicant underwent a material name change more than one year before applying on Form DS-11 and has not updated their ID to reflect the new name, passport personnel must suspend the application and request acceptable ID in the new name.

source_spans.quote: If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name.

units.meaning: Applicants whose material name change occurred within one year of applying on Form DS-11 are exempt from submitting identification showing the new name.

source_spans.quote: Applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name.
